honestLimits: Relation-by-text-mention is deliberate but it is a heuristic: an assertion that names a defined term is treated as related to that term's definition. It cannot tell a correct use of the term from an incorrect one - it establishes topical relation, not semantic correctness. That is the right scope for a grounding layer and it is not an attribution system.

The preserved corpus contains zero context-grounded assertions, so it could not exercise this change at all. The evidence that R2 works is the live 7.2(f) measurement and the synthetic matrix, not the corpus replay.

An assertion whose supporting definition the compiler never retrieved is still UNGROUNDED. That is correct on that compilation's own evidence, but it means grounding quality depends on the compiler's retrieval behaviour, which this mission did not touch.
